title: Liquidity-Adjusted VaR and Cost of Liquidation

maps.tested: Named in a pinned 'please repeat' list alongside RAROC and BCVA, and reported as an explicit numerical in at least two separate sittings. Appears in virtually every recent recall set.
maps.specifics: Reported: '1 numerical on liquidity adjusted VaR'; 'liquidity var numerical'; 'CAR, LVaR'. Two constructions must be kept apart: the constant-spread approach (add 1/2 x spread x position) and the exogenous-spread approach using the spread's own mean and volatility: stressed cost of liquidation = 0.5 x V x (mean spread + z x sd of spread). Picking the wrong one is the sibling swap.

vardeezReading: LTR-1: Important. "Calculation of liquidity trading risk LVAR calculation. Second is liquidity black holes and positive feedback traders". LTR-2: Not so imp. "Calculation of expected transaction cost".

selectors.name: LVaR with normal-market (constant-spread) cost
selectors.what: LVaR = VaR + cost of liquidation in a normal market, where the cost is the sum over positions of (current proportional spread x position value) / 2; includes the 'CAR, LVaR' pairing in which LVaR is asked next to capital at risk.
selectors.theory: Why LVaR is VaR plus the unwinding cost: VaR captures mark-to-market price moves while the cost of liquidation assumes market prices do not change; sells are done at the bid and buys at the offer around the mid price, so each trade costs half the spread.

selectors.name: Stressed (exogenous-spread) cost of liquidation
selectors.what: Stressed cost = sum over positions of (mean spread + lambda x standard deviation of spread) x position value / 2, with lambda = 2.326 at 99% if spreads are normal; the current-spread (constant-spread) input is the sibling-swap distractor.
selectors.theory: Why the stressed cost replaces the current spread by mean plus lambda standard deviations of the proportional spread, why lambda may be set from the empirical distribution because spreads are not normal, and why the stressed cost can be several times the normal-market cost.

selectors.name: Cost of liquidation as its own number
selectors.what: The cost of liquidation alone, not added to VaR: sum of s_i x alpha_i / 2 in a normal market, or sum of (mean + lambda x sd) x alpha_i / 2 in a stressed market; the plain form of the August recall.
selectors.theory: Half the proportional spread is charged on each position's mid-market value; the cost is not the LVaR and is the increment added to VaR, not the adjusted VaR.

selectors.name: LVaR theory: spread, correlation, horizon
selectors.what: Conceptual questions on the two LVaR definitions (normal versus stressed spread), the assumption of perfect correlation of spreads across instruments, and the effect of the liquidation horizon on spread cost and market-move risk.

selectors.name: Malz expected transactions cost, 99% spread factor
selectors.what: Relative spread s = (ask - bid) / midprice; expected transactions cost = 0.5 x s x P per unit; 99% transactions cost = P x 0.5 x (s + 2.33 x sigma_s) per unit, multiplied by the units held.
selectors.theory: Daily changes in the relative spread are normal with zero mean and constant variance, the spread is set at its latest observed value; the expected cost is the half spread, and the 99% spread risk factor is the worst-case bid-ask cost of changing a position, with the one half applying to both the spread and the 2.33 sigma term.

selectors.name: Malz multi-day liquidation adjustment
selectors.what: LVaR over T days = one-day VaR x sqrt((1 + T)(1 + 2T) / (6T)), with T taken as the time to escape from position size against the daily trading volume (T = 5 gives 1.4832, T = 10 about 1.96).
selectors.theory: Liquidating in equal parts means holding 1, (T-1)/T, ..., 1/T of the position, so the adjustment lies between the one-day VaR and one-day VaR x sqrt(T), not equal to sqrt(T).

selectors.name: Liquidity black holes and positive feedback trading
selectors.source: Vardeez: 'Liquidity black holes and positive feedback traders'
selectors.what: Why liquidity dries up when everyone wants to sell (a crowded exit) and the causes of positive feedback trading (trend trading, stop-loss rules, dynamic hedging of short option positions, synthetic options, margin calls, predatory trading); negative feedback traders stabilise, positive feedback traders destabilise.

notSelected: LTR-1 b (liquidity funding risk examples and cases), LTR-1 c (Basel III liquidity ratios, covered under A32), LTR-2 a to d and g (sources of liquidity risk, ALM, collateral markets, leverage, interactions and systemic risk) and the funding-liquidity measurement part of LTR-2 e carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer.
